sanskrit: tām abravīn mahātejā hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ śirasy añjalim ādhāya sītāṃ madhurayā girā
english: Then the great-spirited Hanūmān, son of the Wind, addressed her — Sītā — with a sweet voice, placing his joined hands upon his head.

sanskrit: kā nu padmapalāśākṣī kliṣṭakauśeyavāsinī drumasya śākhām ālambya tiṣṭhasi tvam aninditā
english: Who are you, O blameless one with lotus-petal eyes, clad in soiled silk, who stands clinging to the branch of a tree?

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ tava netrābhyāṃ vāri sravati śokajam puṇḍarīkapalāśābhyāṃ viprakīrṇam ivodakam
english: Why does water born of grief flow from your two eyes — like water scattered from the petals of white lotus flowers?

sanskrit: surāṇām asurāṇāṃ ca nāgagandharvarakṣasām yakṣāṇāṃ kiṃnarāṇāṃ ca kā tvaṃ bhavasi śobhane
english: O fair one, are you of the gods, the asuras, the nāgas, the gandharvas, the rākṣasas, the yakṣas, or the kiṃnaras — which of these do you belong to?

sanskrit: kā tvaṃ bhavasi rudrāṇāṃ marutāṃ vā varānane vasūnāṃ vā varārohe devatā pratibhāsi me
english: O lovely-faced one, O shapely one — are you of the Rudras, or of the Maruts, or of the Vasus? You appear to me a divine being.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu candramasā hīnā patitā vibudhālayāt rohiṇī jyotiṣāṃ śreṣṭhā śreṣṭhā sarvaguṇānvitā
english: Or could you be Rohiṇī, chief among the asterisms, endowed with every virtue, fallen from the celestial abode, separated from the Moon?

sanskrit: kopād vā yadi vā mohād bhartāram asitekṣaṇa vasiṣṭhaṃ kopayitvā tvaṃ nāsi kalyāṇy arundhatī
english: O dark-eyed one, O auspicious one — could you be Arundhatī, who having angered her husband Vasiṣṭha in wrath or delusion, is no longer with him?

sanskrit: ko nau putraḥ pitā bhrāta bhartā vā te sumadhyame asmāl lokād amuṃ lokaṃ gataṃ tvam anuśocasi
english: O slender-waisted one, which son, father, brother, or husband of yours — gone from this world to the other — do you grieve for?

sanskrit: vyañjanāni hi te yāni lakṣaṇāni ca lakṣaye mahiṣī bhūmipālasya rājakanyāsi me matā
english: For the marks and auspicious signs that I observe on you lead me to believe that you are the chief queen or the daughter of a king.

sanskrit: rāvaṇena janasthānād balād apahṛtā yadi sītā tvam asi bhadraṃ te tan mamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ
english: If you are Sītā, forcibly carried away from Janasthāna by Rāvaṇa — good fortune to you — then tell me, for I am asking.

sanskrit: sā tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā rāmakīrtanaharṣitā uvāca vākyaṃ vaidehī hanūmantaṃ drumāśritam
english: She — Vaidehī — hearing his words, gladdened by the mention of Rāma's name, spoke these words to Hanūmān who sat in the tree.

sanskrit: duhitā janakasyāhaṃ vaidehasya mahātmanaḥ sītā ca nāma nāmnāhaṃ bhāryā rāmasya dhīmataḥ
english: "I am the daughter of Janaka, the great-souled king of Videha; by name I am called Sītā, and I am the wife of the wise Rāma."

sanskrit: samā dvādaśa tatrāhaṃ rāghavasya niveśane bhuñjānā mānuṣān bhogān sarvakāmasamṛddhinī
english: "For twelve years I dwelt in the household of Rāghava, enjoying human pleasures, fulfilled in every desire."

sanskrit: tatas trayodaśe varṣe rājyenekṣvākunandanam abhiṣecayituṃ rājā sopādhyāyaḥ pracakrame
english: "Then in the thirteenth year, the king, together with his preceptors, began the preparations to consecrate the delight of the Ikṣvākus with the kingdom."

sanskrit: tasmin saṃbhriyamāṇe tu rāghavasyābhiṣecane kaikeyī nāma bhartāraṃ devī vacanam abravīt
english: "But while those preparations for Rāghava's consecration were being assembled, the queen named Kaikeyī spoke these words to her husband."

sanskrit: na pibeyaṃ na khādeyaṃ pratyahaṃ mama bhojanam eṣa me jīvitasyānto rāmo yady abhiṣicyate
english: "'I shall neither drink nor eat — this is the end of my life each day — if Rāma is consecrated.'"

sanskrit: yat tad uktaṃ tvayā vākyaṃ prītyā nṛpatisattama tac cen na vitathaṃ kāryaṃ vanaṃ gacchatu rāghavaḥ
english: "'If that promise spoken by you with affection, O best of kings, is not to be made false, then let Rāghava go to the forest.'"

sanskrit: sa rājā satyavāg devyā varadānam anusmaran mumoha vacanaṃ śrutvā kaikeyyāḥ krūram apriyam
english: "That king, ever true to his word, recalling the boon granted to the queen, fainted upon hearing Kaikeyī's cruel and disagreeable words."

sanskrit: tatas tu sthaviro rājā satyadharme vyavasthitaḥ jyeṣṭhaṃ yaśasvinaṃ putraṃ rudan rājyam ayācata
english: "Then that aged king, steadfast in truth and righteousness, weeping, begged his eldest and glorious son to accept the kingdom."

sanskrit: sa pitur vacanaṃ śrīmān abhiṣekāt paraṃ priyam manasā pūrvam āsādya vācā pratigṛhītavān
english: "He — the glorious one — having first accepted in his mind the father's word, which was dearer than the consecration itself, accepted it with his speech."

sanskrit: dadyān na pratigṛhṇīyān na brūyat kiṃ cid apriyam api jīvitahetor hi rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
english: "Rāma, whose valor lies in truth, would give but never take, and would not say anything disagreeable — even for the sake of his own life."

sanskrit: sa vihāyottarīyāṇi mahārhāṇi mahāyaśāḥ visṛjya manasā rājyaṃ jananyai māṃ samādiśat
english: "He — the greatly renowned — casting off his precious upper garments and renouncing the kingdom in his heart, entrusted me to his mother."

sanskrit: sāhaṃ tasyāgratas tūrṇaṃ prasthitā vanacāriṇī na hi me tena hīnāyā vāsaḥ svarge 'pi rocate
english: "And I, quickly setting out before him as a wanderer of the forest — for to me, separated from him, even heaven is not pleasing."

sanskrit: prāg eva tu mahābhāgaḥ saumitrir mitranandanaḥ pūrvajasyānuyātrārthe drumacīrair alaṃkṛtaḥ
english: "And before us, the greatly fortunate Saumitri, the joy of his friends, had adorned himself with bark-cloth garments to accompany his elder brother."

sanskrit: te vayaṃ bhartur ādeśaṃ bahu mānyadṛḍhavratāḥ praviṣṭāḥ sma purād dṛṣṭaṃ vanaṃ gambhīradarśanam
english: "We three, honoring the command of the husband and firm in our vows, entered from the city into the forest — vast and deep in appearance."

sanskrit: vasato daṇḍakāraṇye tasyāham amitaujasaḥ rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā rāvaṇena durātmanā
english: "While I was dwelling with him — that one of boundless might — in the Daṇḍaka forest, I, his wife, was abducted by the rākṣasa Rāvaṇa, of evil soul."

sanskrit: dvau māsau tena me kālo jīvitānugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ ūrdhvaṃ dvābhyāṃ tu māsābhyāṃ tatas tyakṣyāmi jīvitam
english: "By him a term of two months was granted to me as a favor to preserve my life; but beyond those two months, I shall then abandon my life."

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā hanūmān hariyūthapaḥ duḥkhād duḥkhābhibhūtāyāḥ sāntam uttaram abravīt
english: Hearing those words of hers — overwhelmed with grief upon grief — Hanūmān, leader of the monkey host, spoke a soothing reply.

sanskrit: ahaṃ rāmasya saṃdeśād devi dūtas tavāgataḥ vaidehi kuśalī rāmas tvāṃ ca kauśalam abravīt
english: "O goddess, I have come to you as a messenger bearing Rāma's tidings. O Vaidehī, Rāma is well, and he has conveyed his welfare to you."

sanskrit: yo brāhmam astraṃ vedāṃś ca veda vedavidāṃ varaḥ sa tvāṃ dāśarathī rāmo devi kauśalam abravīt
english: "He who knows the Brahmā-weapon and the Vedas, the foremost among those who know the Vedas — that Rāma, son of Daśaratha, O goddess, has conveyed his welfare to you."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaś ca mahātejā bhartus te 'nucaraḥ priyaḥ kṛtavāñ śokasaṃtaptaḥ śirasā te 'bhivādanam
english: "And Lakṣmaṇa, of great splendor, the beloved attendant of your husband, scorched with grief, has made obeisance to you with his head."

sanskrit: sā tayoḥ kuśalaṃ devī niśamya narasiṃhayoḥ prītisaṃhṛṣṭasarvāṅgī hanūmāntam athābravīt
english: She — the goddess — hearing the welfare of those two lion-like men, with all her limbs thrilling with joy and delight, then spoke to Hanūmān.

sanskrit: kalyāṇī bata gatheyaṃ laukikī pratibhāti me ehi jīvantam ānado naraṃ varṣaśatād api
english: "Truly this common saying seems to me auspicious: 'One meets a living man with joy even after a hundred years.'"

sanskrit: tayoḥ samāgame tasmin prītir utpāditādbhutā paraspareṇa cālāpaṃ viśvastau tau pracakratuḥ
english: In that encounter between the two of them, a wondrous joy arose; and trusting each other, the two began a mutual conversation.

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā hanūmān hariyūthapaḥ sītāyāḥ śokadīnāyāḥ samīpam upacakrame
english: Hearing those words of hers, Hanūmān, leader of the monkey host, drew near to Sītā, who was wasted with grief.

sanskrit: yathā yathā samīpaṃ sa hanūmān upasarpati tathā tathā rāvaṇaṃ sā taṃ sītā pariśaṅkate
english: The more Hanūmān crept closer to her, the more Sītā suspected him to be Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: aho dhig dhig kṛtam idaṃ kathitaṃ hi yad asya me rūpāntaram upāgamya sa evāyaṃ hi rāvaṇaḥ
english: "Alas, shame, shame — what I have done! For what I told him about myself — having assumed a different form, this is surely Rāvaṇa himself."

sanskrit: tām aśokasya śākhāṃ sā vimuktvā śokakarśitā tasyām evānavadyāṅgī dharaṇyāṃ samupāviśat
english: She — the flawless-limbed one, wasted with grief — releasing that branch of the aśoka tree, sat down upon the very ground beneath it.

sanskrit: avandata mahābāhus tatas tāṃ janakātmajām sā cainaṃ bhayavitrastā bhūyo naivābhyudaikṣata
english: Then the long-armed one bowed down to that daughter of Janaka; but she, trembling with fear, did not look up at him again.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vandamānaṃ tu sītā śaśinibhānanā abravīd dīrgham ucchvasya vānaraṃ madhurasvarā
english: Seeing him bowing, Sītā — whose face was like the moon — having drawn a long breath, spoke to that monkey in a sweet voice.

sanskrit: māyāṃ praviṣṭo māyāvī yadi tvaṃ rāvaṇaḥ svayam utpādayasi me bhūyaḥ saṃtāpaṃ tan na śobhanam
english: "If you are Rāvaṇa himself, a master of illusion who has entered into illusion, you are again creating anguish for me — that is not right."

sanskrit: svaṃ parityajya rūpaṃ yaḥ parivrājakarūpadhṛt janasthāne mayā dṛṣṭas tvaṃ sa evāsi rāvaṇaḥ
english: "You who abandoned your own form and took the guise of an ascetic wanderer — you are that very Rāvaṇa I saw in Janasthāna."

sanskrit: upavāsakṛśāṃ dīnāṃ kāmarūpa niśācara saṃtāpayasi māṃ bhūyaḥ saṃtāpaṃ tan na śobhanam
english: "O night-roaming shapeshifter, you torment me again — thin from fasting and wretched as I am. That is not right."

sanskrit: yadi rāmasya dūtas tvam āgato bhadram astu te pṛcchāmi tvāṃ hariśreṣṭha priyā rāma kathā hi me
english: "But if you have truly come as Rāma's messenger — good fortune to you! I ask you, O foremost of monkeys, for the story of Rāma is dear to me."

sanskrit: guṇān rāmasya kathaya priyasya mama vānara cittaṃ harasi me saumya nadīkūlaṃ yathā rayaḥ
english: "Tell me the virtues of Rāma, my beloved, O monkey. You steal away my heart, O gentle one, as a current steals away a riverbank."

sanskrit: aho svapnasya sukhatā yāham evaṃ cirāhṛtā preṣitaṃ nāma paśyāmi rāghaveṇa vanaukasaṃ
english: "Ah, how sweet is a dream! — I who have been carried away for so long, now seem to see a forest-dweller sent by Rāghava."

sanskrit: svapne 'pi yady ahaṃ vīraṃ rāghavaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam paśyeyaṃ nāvasīdeyaṃ svapno 'pi mama matsarī
english: "Even if I were to see the heroic Rāghava along with Lakṣmaṇa only in a dream, I would not sink into despair — even a dream begrudges me this."

sanskrit: nāhaṃ svapnam imaṃ manye svapne dṛṣṭvā hi vānaram na śakyo 'bhyudayaḥ prāptuṃ prāptaś cābhyudayo mama
english: "But I do not think this is a dream — for in a dream one cannot attain good fortune by seeing a monkey; and yet good fortune has come to me."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu syāc cittamoho 'yaṃ bhaved vātagatis tv iyam unmādajo vikāro vā syād iyaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇikā
english: "Could this be a confusion of the mind? Or is this a phantom of the wind? Or could this be a disorder arising from madness? Or is this a mirage?"

sanskrit: atha vā nāyam unmādo moho 'py unmādalakṣmaṇaḥ saṃbudhye cāham ātmānam imaṃ cāpi vanaukasaṃ
english: "Or else, this is not madness, nor is this confusion bearing the marks of madness — for I am fully conscious of myself and of this forest-dweller as well."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ bahudhā sītā saṃpradhārya balābalam rakṣasāṃ kāmarūpatvān mene taṃ rākṣasādhipam
english: Thus reflecting in many ways upon the pros and cons, Sītā, because of the rākṣasas' power of taking any form at will, took him to be the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ tadā kṛtvā sītā sā tanumadhyamā na prativyājahārātha vānaraṃ janakātmajā
english: Having arrived at this conclusion then, that slender-waisted Sītā, daughter of Janaka, did not reply to the monkey.

sanskrit: sītāyāś cintitaṃ buddhvā hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ śrotrānukūlair vacanais tadā tāṃ saṃpraharṣayat
english: Knowing what Sītā was thinking, Hanūmān, son of the Wind, then delighted her with words pleasing to the ears.

sanskrit: āditya iva tejasvī lokakāntaḥ śaśī yathā rājā sarvasya lokasya devo vaiśravaṇo yathā
english: "Rāma is radiant as the sun, beloved of the world as the moon, the king of all the world, like the god Vaiśravaṇa —

sanskrit: vikrameṇopapannaś ca yathā viṣṇur mahāyaśāḥ satyavādī madhuravāg devo vācaspatir yathā
english: endowed with valor like the greatly glorious Viṣṇu, a speaker of truth with sweet speech like the god Bṛhaspati —

sanskrit: rūpavān subhagaḥ śrīmān kandarpa iva mūrtimān sthānakrodhaprahartā ca śreṣṭho loke mahārathaḥ bāhucchāyām avaṣṭabdho yasya loko mahātmanaḥ
english: handsome, fortunate, glorious, like Kandarpa in embodied form, skilled in striking anger at the right place, the foremost great chariot-warrior in the world — the world rests within the shelter of the arms of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: apakṛṣyāśramapadān mṛgarūpeṇa rāghavam śūnye yenāpanītāsi tasya drakṣyasi yat phalam
english: "You shall see the fruit that awaits him by whom Rāghava was lured away from the hermitage in the guise of a deer, and you were carried off in the empty forest."

sanskrit: nacirād rāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye yo vadhiṣyati vīryavān roṣapramuktair iṣubhir jvaladbhir iva pāvakaiḥ
english: "He of great valor will, before long, slay Rāvaṇa in battle with blazing arrows released in fury, burning like fire."

sanskrit: tenāhaṃ preṣito dūtas tvatsakāśam ihāgataḥ tvadviyogena duḥkhārtaḥ sa tvāṃ kauśalam abravīt
english: "By him I have been sent as a messenger and have come here to your side; he, afflicted with grief from separation from you, has conveyed his welfare to you."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaś ca mahātejāḥ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ abhivādya mahābāhuḥ so 'pi kauśalam abravīt
english: "And Lakṣmaṇa of great splendor, the increaser of Sumitrā's joy, the long-armed one — he too, having paid his respects, has conveyed his welfare to you."

sanskrit: rāmasya ca sakhā devi sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ rājā vānaramukhyānāṃ sa tvāṃ kauśalam abravīt
english: "And the friend of Rāma, O goddess — a monkey named Sugrīva, king of the foremost monkeys — he too has conveyed his welfare to you."

sanskrit: nityaṃ smarati rāmas tvāṃ sasugrīvaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ diṣṭyā jīvasi vaidehi rākṣasī vaśam āgatā
english: "Rāma constantly remembers you, together with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa. By good fortune you live, O Vaidehī, though fallen into the power of the rākṣasī."

sanskrit: nacirād drakṣyase rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahāratham madhye vānarakoṭīnāṃ sugrīvaṃ cāmitaujasaṃ
english: "Before long you will see Rāma, and Lakṣmaṇa the great chariot-warrior, in the midst of tens of millions of monkeys, and Sugrīva of boundless might."

sanskrit: ahaṃ sugrīvasacivo hanūmān nāma vānaraḥ praviṣṭo nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ laṅghayitvā mahodadhim
english: "I am a monkey named Hanūmān, minister of Sugrīva. Having leapt across the great ocean, I have entered the city of Laṅkā."

sanskrit: kṛtvā mūrdhni padanyāsaṃ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ tvāṃ draṣṭum upayāto 'haṃ samāśritya parākramam
english: "Placing my foot upon the head of the evil-souled Rāvaṇa, I have come to see you, relying upon my own valor."

sanskrit: nāham asmi tathā devi yathā mām avagacchasi viśaṅkā tyajyatām eṣā śraddhatsva vadato mama
english: "O goddess, I am not what you take me to be. Let this suspicion be abandoned; trust the words I speak to you."

sanskrit: tāṃ tu rāma kathāṃ śrutvā vaidehī vānararṣabhāt uvāca vacanaṃ sāntvam idaṃ madhurayā girā
english: But Vaidehī, having heard those words about Rāma from that bull among monkeys, spoke this soothing speech in a sweet voice.

sanskrit: kva te rāmeṇa saṃsargaḥ kathaṃ jānāsi lakṣmaṇam vānarāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca katham āsīt samāgamaḥ
english: "What is your connection with Rāma? How do you know Lakṣmaṇa? How did the meeting of monkeys and men come about?"

sanskrit: yāni rāmasya liṅgāni lakṣmaṇasya ca vānara tāni bhūyaḥ samācakṣva na māṃ śokaḥ samāviśet
english: "O monkey, describe once more the distinguishing marks of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, so that grief may not overwhelm me."

sanskrit: kīdṛśaṃ tasya saṃsthānaṃ rūpaṃ rāmasya kīdṛśam katham ūrū kathaṃ bāhū lakṣmaṇasya ca śaṃsa me
english: "What is his bearing, what is Rāma's form? What are his thighs like, what are his arms like? Tell me also of Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu vaidehyā hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ tato rāmaṃ yathātattvam ākhyātum upacakrame
english: Thus addressed by Vaidehī, Hanūmān, son of the Wind, then proceeded to describe Rāma truthfully and accurately.

sanskrit: jānantī bata diṣṭyā māṃ vaidehi paripṛcchasi bhartuḥ kamalapatrākṣi saṃkhyānaṃ lakṣmaṇasya ca
english: "By good fortune, O Vaidehī, O lotus-eyed one, though knowing me, you yet ask me — about the description of your husband and of Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: yāni rāmasya cihnāni lakṣmaṇasya ca yāni vai lakṣitāni viśālākṣi vadataḥ śṛṇu tāni me
english: "O wide-eyed one, hear from me as I speak of those identifying marks of Rāma and of Lakṣmaṇa as they have been observed."

sanskrit: rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣaḥ sarvabhūtamanoharaḥ rūpadākṣiṇyasaṃpannaḥ prasūto janakātmaje
english: "Rāma is lotus-petal-eyed, captivating the hearts of all beings, endowed with beauty and grace, O daughter of Janaka."

sanskrit: tejasādityasaṃkāśaḥ kṣamayā pṛthivīsamaḥ bṛhaspatisamo buddhyā yaśasā vāsavopamaḥ
english: "In brilliance he is like the sun, in forbearance equal to the earth, in wisdom equal to Bṛhaspati, in glory comparable to Vāsava."

sanskrit: rakṣitā jīvalokasya svajanasya ca rakṣitā rakṣitā svasya vṛttasya dharmasya ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: "He is the protector of the living world, the protector of his own people, the protector of his own conduct and of dharma — the scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: rāmo bhāmini lokasya cāturvarṇyasya rakṣitā maryādānāṃ ca lokasya kartā kārayitā ca saḥ
english: "O passionate one, Rāma is the protector of the four social orders of the world, and the maker and enforcer of the boundaries of the world."

sanskrit: arciṣmān arcito 'tyarthaṃ brahmacaryavrate sthitaḥ sādhūnām upakārajñaḥ pracārajñaś ca karmaṇām
english: "Radiant and greatly honored, established in the vow of brahmacarya, he knows how to assist the virtuous and knows the conduct of duties."

sanskrit: rājavidyāvinītaś ca brāhmaṇānām upāsitā śrutavāñ śīlasaṃpanno vinītaś ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: "Trained in the science of kingship, a devoted attendant upon brāhmaṇas, learned in scripture, endowed with good character, and disciplined — he is a scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: yajurvedavinītaś ca vedavidbhiḥ supūjitaḥ dhanurvede ca vede ca vedāṅgeṣu ca niṣṭhitaḥ
english: "Learned in the Yajurveda, greatly honored by those who know the Vedas, he is established in the science of archery, in the Vedas, and in the Vedāṅgas."

sanskrit: vipulāṃso mahābāhuḥ kambugrīvaḥ śubhānanaḥ gūḍhajatruḥ sutāmrākṣo rāmo devi janaiḥ śrutaḥ
english: "Broad-shouldered, long-armed, with a neck like a conch-shell, of auspicious countenance, with well-concealed collar-bones, reddish-brown eyes — thus is Rāma celebrated among the people, O goddess."

sanskrit: dundubhisvananirghoṣaḥ snigdhavarṇaḥ pratāpavān samaḥ samavibhaktāṅgo varṇaṃ śyāmaṃ samāśritaḥ
english: "His voice resounds like a kettledrum, his complexion is lustrous, he is of great majesty, his limbs are even and well-proportioned, and his color is dark (śyāma)."

sanskrit: tristhiras tripralambaś ca trisamas triṣu connataḥ trivalīvāṃs tryavaṇataś caturvyaṅgas triśīrṣavān
english: "He has three prominences, three extensions, three levels; he is elevated in three places; he bears three folds, is bent down in three; has four outer limbs well-developed and three crown-points."

sanskrit: catuṣkalaś caturlekhaś catuṣkiṣkuś catuḥsamaḥ caturdaśasamadvandvaś caturdaṣṭaś caturgatiḥ
english: "He has four sections, four lines, four cubits' measure; he is fourfold equal; fourteen pairs of limbs proportionate; four types of teeth; four gaits."

sanskrit: mahauṣṭhahanunāsaś ca pañcasnigdho 'ṣṭavaṃśavān daśapadmo daśabṛhat tribhir vyāpto dviśuklavān ṣaḍunnato navatanus tribhir vyāpnoti rāghavaḥ
english: "Great in lips, cheeks, and nose; smooth in five places; eight-ribbed; bearing ten lotus-marks; ten great qualities; pervaded by three; doubly bright; elevated in six places; slender in nine — thus Rāghava extends through three dimensions."

sanskrit: satyadharmaparaḥ śrīmān saṃgrahānugrahe rataḥ deśakālavibhāgajñaḥ sarvalokapriyaṃvadaḥ
english: "Supreme in truth and dharma, glorious, devoted to gathering allies and showing grace, knowing the distinctions of place and time, speaking pleasingly to all the world."

sanskrit: bhrātā ca tasya dvaimātraḥ saumitrir aparājitaḥ anurāgeṇa rūpeṇa guṇaiś caiva tathāvidhaḥ
english: "And his brother of different mother, the unvanquished Saumitri — in affection, in form, and in virtues he is of the same kind."

sanskrit: tvām eva mārgamāṇo tau vicarantau vasuṃdharām dadarśatur mṛgapatiṃ pūrvajenāvaropitam
english: "Those two, wandering the earth in search of you alone, encountered the lord of beasts who had been cast down by his elder brother."

sanskrit: ṛśyamūkasya pṛṣṭhe tu bahupādapasaṃkule bhrātur bhāryārtam āsīnaṃ sugrīvaṃ priyadarśanam
english: "On the slopes of Ṛśyamūka, dense with many trees, they found Sugrīva of pleasing appearance, seated, bereft of his brother's wife."

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu harirājaṃ taṃ sugrīvaṃ satyasaṃgaram paricaryāmahe rājyāt pūrvajenāvaropitam
english: "And we served that king of monkeys, Sugrīva, true to his pledges, who had been expelled from the kingdom by his elder brother."

sanskrit: tatas tau cīravasanau dhanuḥpravarapāṇinau ṛśyamūkasya śailasya ramyaṃ deśam upāgatau
english: "Then those two, clad in bark-cloth garments, holding excellent bows in hand, came to a beautiful region of the Ṛśyamūka mountain."

sanskrit: sa tau dṛṣṭvā naravyāghrau dhanvinau vānararṣabhaḥ abhipluto gires tasya śikharaṃ bhayamohitaḥ
english: "Seeing those two tiger-like men with bows, that bull among monkeys leapt up to the peak of that mountain, bewildered with fear."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa śikhare tasmin vānarendro vyavasthitaḥ tayoḥ samīpaṃ mām eva preṣayām āsa satvaraḥ
english: "Then that lord of monkeys, stationed on that peak, hastily sent me alone to those two."

sanskrit: tāv ahaṃ puruṣavyāghrau sugrīvavacanāt prabhū rūpalakṣaṇasaṃpannau kṛtāñjalir upasthitaḥ
english: "I, by the word of Sugrīva, with joined hands approached those two tiger-like lords of men, endowed with fine form and auspicious marks."

sanskrit: tau parijñātatattvārthau mayā prītisamanvitau pṛṣṭham āropya taṃ deśaṃ prāpitau puruṣarṣabhau
english: "Those two bull-like men, whose true purpose I had come to know, being filled with joy, I brought to that place, having set them upon my back."

sanskrit: niveditau ca tattvena sugrīvāya mahātmane tayor anyonyasaṃbhāṣād bhṛśaṃ prītir ajāyata
english: "And having introduced them truly to the great-souled Sugrīva, from their mutual conversation intense joy arose between them."

sanskrit: tatra tau kīrtisaṃpannau harīśvaranareśvarau parasparakṛtāśvāsau kathayā pūrvavṛttayā
english: "There those two — endowed with glory, the lord of monkeys and the lord of men — each reassuring the other, spoke of past events."

sanskrit: taṃ tataḥ sāntvayām āsa sugrīvaṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ strīhetor vālinā bhrātrā nirastam uru tejasā
english: "Then the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa comforted Sugrīva, who had been expelled by his brother Vālin — of immense energy — on account of a woman."

sanskrit: tatas tvan nāśajaṃ śokaṃ rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ lakṣmaṇo vānarendrāya sugrīvāya nyavedayat
english: "Then Lakṣmaṇa reported to Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, the grief born of your disappearance — the grief of Rāma of untiring deeds."

sanskrit: sa śrutvā vānarendras tu lakṣmaṇeneritaṃ vacaḥ tadāsīn niṣprabho 'tyarthaṃ grahagrasta ivāṃśumān
english: "That lord of monkeys, hearing the words spoken by Lakṣmaṇa, became utterly lustrous-less then, like the sun seized by a planet."

sanskrit: tatas tvadgātraśobhīni rakṣasā hriyamāṇayā yāny ābharaṇajālāni pātitāni mahītale
english: "Then the masses of ornaments that adorned your body, which had fallen to the earth as you were being carried off by the rākṣasa —"

sanskrit: tāni sarvāṇi rāmāya ānīya hariyūthapāḥ saṃhṛṣṭā darśayām āsur gatiṃ tu na vidus tava
english: "— all of those the monkey troop leaders brought to Rāma and joyfully showed him, but they did not know the direction you had gone."

sanskrit: tāni rāmāya dattāni mayaivopahṛtāni ca svanavanty avakīrṇanti tasmin vihatacetasi
english: "Those ornaments given to Rāma, brought by me and placed before him — they were sounding and strewn about upon that one whose mind was shattered."

sanskrit: tāny aṅke darśanīyāni kṛtvā bahuvidhaṃ tataḥ tena devaprakāśena devena paridevitam
english: "Having placed those beautiful ornaments in his lap, that god-like one then lamented in many ways."

sanskrit: paśyatas tasyā rudatas tāmyataś ca punaḥ punaḥ prādīpayan dāśarathes tāni śokahutāśanam
english: "Looking at them, weeping, fainting again and again — those ornaments fed the fire of grief of that son of Daśaratha."

sanskrit: śayitaṃ ca ciraṃ tena duḥkhārtena mahātmanā mayāpi vividhair vākyaiḥ kṛcchrād utthāpitaḥ punaḥ
english: "That great-souled one, tormented with grief, lay prostrate for a long time; and even I with difficulty raised him up again with various words."

sanskrit: tāni dṛṣṭvā mahārhāṇi darśayitvā muhur muhuḥ rāghavaḥ sahasaumitriḥ sugrīve sa nyavedayat
english: "Having seen those precious ornaments and shown them again and again, Rāghava, together with Saumitri, reported to Sugrīva."

sanskrit: sa tavādarśanād ārye rāghavaḥ paritapyate mahatā jvalatā nityam agninevāgniparvataḥ
english: "He — Rāghava — burns constantly from not seeing you, O noble one, with a great blazing fire, like a fire-mountain with fire."

sanskrit: tvatkṛte tam anidrā ca śokaś cintā ca rāghavam tāpayanti mahātmānam agnyagāram ivāgnayaḥ
english: "On your account, sleeplessness, grief, and anxiety torment that great-souled Rāghava, as fires torment a fire-chamber."

sanskrit: tavādarśanaśokena rāghavaḥ pravicālyate mahatā bhūmikampena mahān iva śiloccayaḥ
english: "From grief at not seeing you, Rāghava is shaken, as a great mountain of rock is shaken by a great earthquake."

sanskrit: kānānāni suramyāṇi nadīprasravaṇāni ca caran na ratim āpnoti tvam apaśyan nṛpātmaje
english: "Wandering through lovely forest groves and river springs, he finds no delight, not seeing you, O daughter of a king."

sanskrit: sa tvāṃ manujaśārdūlaḥ kṣipraṃ prāpsyati rāghavaḥ samitrabāndhavaṃ hatvā rāvaṇaṃ janakātmaje
english: "He — Rāghava, that tiger among men — will come to you quickly, O daughter of Janaka, having slain Rāvaṇa together with his allies and kinsmen."

sanskrit: sahitau rāmasugrīvāv ubhāv akurutāṃ tadā samayaṃ vālinaṃ hantuṃ tava cānveṣaṇaṃ tathā
english: "Together, Rāma and Sugrīva both then made a compact — to slay Vālin and likewise to search for you."

sanskrit: tato nihatya tarasā rāmo vālinam āhave sarvarkṣaharisaṃghānāṃ sugrīvam akarot patim
english: "Then Rāma, having swiftly slain Vālin in battle, made Sugrīva lord of all the hosts of bears and monkeys."

sanskrit: rāmasugrīvayor aikyaṃ devy evaṃ samajāyata hanūmantaṃ ca māṃ viddhi tayor dūtam ihāgatam
english: "O goddess, thus was the union of Rāma and Sugrīva brought about. And know me, Hanūmān, to have come here as the messenger of those two."

sanskrit: svarājyaṃ prāpya sugrīvaḥ samanīya mahāharīn tvadarthaṃ preṣayām āsa diśo daśa mahābalān
english: "Having obtained his own kingdom, Sugrīva assembled the great monkeys and dispatched them, the greatly powerful ones, in all ten directions in search of you."

sanskrit: ādiṣṭā vānarendreṇa sugrīveṇa mahaujasaḥ adrirājapratīkāśāḥ sarvataḥ prasthitā mahīm
english: "Commanded by Sugrīva, lord of monkeys, of immense energy, those monkeys — resembling kings of mountains — set out in all directions across the earth."

sanskrit: aṅgado nāma lakṣmīvān vālisūnur mahābalaḥ prasthitaḥ kapiśārdūlas tribhāgabalasaṃvṛtaḥ
english: "A glorious monkey named Aṅgada, son of Vālin, of great strength — that tiger among monkeys — set out accompanied by a third of the army."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ no vipranaṣṭānāṃ vindhye parvatasattame bhṛśaṃ śokaparītanām ahorātragaṇā gatāḥ
english: "For us, having strayed and lost our way on the great mountain Vindhya, deeply overcome with grief, days and nights passed by."

sanskrit: te vayaṃ kāryanairāśyāt kālasyātikrameṇa ca bhayāc ca kapirājasya prāṇāṃs tyaktuṃ vyavasthitāḥ
english: "We were resolved to abandon our lives — out of despair over our mission, from the lapse of time, and from fear of the monkey king."

sanskrit: vicitya vanadurgāṇi giriprasravaṇāni ca anāsādya padaṃ devyāḥ prāṇāṃs tyaktuṃ vyavasthitāḥ
english: "Having searched through forest fastnesses and mountain streams, and not finding the track of the goddess, we were resolved to abandon our lives."

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ śokārṇave magnaḥ paryadevayad aṅgadaḥ tava nāśaṃ ca vaidehi vālinaś ca tathā vadham prāyopaveśam asmākaṃ maraṇaṃ ca jaṭāyuṣaḥ
english: "Deeply plunged in an ocean of grief, Aṅgada lamented — your disappearance, O Vaidehī, the death of Vālin, our own penance-fast unto death, and the death of Jaṭāyu."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ naḥ svāmisaṃdeśān nirāśānāṃ mumūrṣatām kāryahetor ivāyātaḥ śakunir vīryavān mahān
english: "For us who had lost hope and were ready to die, a great and powerful bird came, as if for the sake of our mission — as if summoned by our lord's command."

sanskrit: gṛdhrarājasya sodaryaḥ saṃpātir nāma gṛdhrarāṭ śrutvā bhrātṛvadhaṃ kopād idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: "The full brother of the king of vultures, a king of vultures named Saṃpāti, hearing of his brother's death, spoke these words in anger."

sanskrit: yavīyān kena me bhrātā hataḥ kva ca vināśitaḥ etad ākhyātum icchāmi bhavadbhir vānarottamāḥ
english: "'By whom was my younger brother slain? Where was he destroyed? I wish you, O best of monkeys, to tell me this.'"

sanskrit: aṅgado 'kathayat tasya janasthāne mahad vadham rakṣasā bhīmarūpeṇa tvām uddiśya yathātatham
english: "Aṅgada told him accurately about the great slaughter in Janasthāna, done by a rākṣasa of terrible form, directed at you."

sanskrit: jaṭāyos tu vadhaṃ śrutvā duḥkhitaḥ so 'ruṇātmajaḥ tvām āha sa varārohe vasantīṃ rāvaṇālaye
english: "That son of Aruṇa, grieved upon hearing of Jaṭāyu's death, told them — O shapely one — that you were dwelling in Rāvaṇa's palace."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā saṃpāteḥ prītivardhanam aṅgadapramukhāḥ sarve tataḥ saṃprasthitā vayam tvaddarśanakṛtotsāhā hṛṣṭās tuṣṭāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: "Hearing those joy-increasing words of Saṃpāti, all of us — with Aṅgada at our head — then set forth, we the leaping ones, thrilled and glad, with enthusiasm born of the desire to see you."

sanskrit: athāhaṃ harisainyasya sāgaraṃ dṛśya sīdataḥ vyavadhūya bhayaṃ tīvraṃ yojanānāṃ śataṃ plutaḥ
english: "Then I, seeing the monkey army sinking in despair before the ocean, shaking off intense fear, leapt a hundred yojanas."

sanskrit: laṅkā cāpi mayā rātrau praviṣṭā rākṣasākulā rāvaṇaś ca mayā dṛṣṭas tvaṃ ca śokanipīḍitā
english: "And Laṅkā, teeming with rākṣasas, was entered by me at night; and Rāvaṇa was seen by me, and you — oppressed with grief."

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathāvṛttam anindite abhibhāṣasva māṃ devi dūto dāśarather aham
english: "All this has been told to you as it occurred, O blameless one. Speak to me, O goddess — I am the messenger of the son of Daśaratha."

sanskrit: tvaṃ māṃ rāmakṛtodyogaṃ tvannimittam ihāgatam sugrīva sacivaṃ devi budhyasva pavanātmajam
english: "Know me, O goddess, to be the Wind-god's son, the minister of Sugrīva — who has exerted himself on Rāma's behalf, and who has come here on your account."

sanskrit: kuśalī tava kākutsthaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ guror ārādhane yukto lakṣmaṇaś ca sulakṣaṇaḥ
english: "Your Kākutstha — foremost among all bearers of weapons — is well, and Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks, devoted to honoring his elder as a guru, is well."

sanskrit: tasya vīryavato devi bhartus tava hite rataḥ aham ekas tu saṃprāptaḥ sugrīvavacanād iha
english: "O goddess, I alone have arrived here by the command of Sugrīva, devoted to the welfare of your husband — that valorous one."

sanskrit: mayeyam asahāyena caratā kāmarūpiṇā dakṣiṇā dig anukrāntā tvanmārgavicayaiṣiṇā
english: "By me — wandering alone, able to take any form at will, searching for your trail — this southern quarter has been traversed."

sanskrit: diṣṭyāhaṃ harisainyānāṃ tvannāśam anuśocatām apaneṣyāmi saṃtāpaṃ tavābhigamaśaṃsanāt
english: "By good fortune, I shall remove the anguish of the monkey army grieving over your loss — by the announcement of my having reached you."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā hi na mama vyarthaṃ devi sāgaralaṅghanam prāpsyāmy aham idaṃ diṣṭyā tvaddarśanakṛtaṃ yaśaḥ
english: "By good fortune, my crossing of the ocean has not been in vain, O goddess; and by good fortune I shall gain this glory earned by having seen you."

sanskrit: rāghavaś ca mahāvīryaḥ kṣipraṃ tvām abhipatsyate samitrabāndhavaṃ hatvā rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam
english: "And Rāghava of great valor will come to you quickly, having slain Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas, together with his allies and kinsmen."

sanskrit: kaurajo nāma vaidehi girīṇām uttamo giriḥ tato gacchati gokarṇaṃ parvataṃ kesarī hariḥ
english: "O Vaidehī, there is a mountain called Kauraja, the best of mountains; from there the monkey Kesarī went to the mountain Gokarṇa."

sanskrit: sa ca devarṣibhir dṛṣṭaḥ pitā mama mahākapiḥ tīrthe nadīpateḥ puṇye śambasādanam uddharat
english: "And that great monkey — my father — was seen by divine sages, as he destroyed the abode of Sāmba at a sacred ford of the lord of rivers."

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ hariṇaḥ kṣetre jāto vātena maithili hanūmān iti vikhyāto loke svenaiva karmaṇā viśvāsārthaṃ tu vaidehi bhartur uktā mayā guṇāḥ
english: "I was born in the field of that monkey by the Wind-god, O Maithilī; and I am known in the world as Hanūmān by my own deeds. And O Vaidehī, the virtues of your husband have been spoken by me for the sake of establishing trust."

sanskrit: evaṃ viśvāsitā sītā hetubhiḥ śokakarśitā upapannair abhijñānair dūtaṃ tam avagacchati
english: Thus Sītā — wasted with grief — being thus reassured with apt proofs of recognition, acknowledged him as the true messenger.

sanskrit: atulaṃ ca gatā harṣaṃ praharṣeṇa tu jānakī netrābhyāṃ vakrapakṣmābhyāṃ mumocānandajaṃ jalam
english: And Jānakī, filled with unmatched joy, from that delight shed tears of happiness from her two eyes with their curling lashes.

sanskrit: cāru tac cānanaṃ tasyās tāmraśuklāyatekṣaṇam aśobhata viśālākṣyā rāhumukta ivoḍurāṭ hanūmantaṃ kapiṃ vyaktaṃ manyate nānyatheti sā
english: That beautiful face of hers — with long eyes of reddish-white hue — shone, that wide-eyed one's face, like the moon freed from Rāhu; and she clearly understood him, that monkey Hanūmān, to be none other than what he said.

sanskrit: athovāca hanūmāṃs tām uttaraṃ priyadarśanām
english: Then Hanūmān spoke a further word to that fair-visaged one.

sanskrit: hate 'sure saṃyati śambasādane kapipravīreṇa maharṣicodanāt tato 'smi vāyuprabhavo hi maithili prabhāvatas tatpratimaś ca vānaraḥ
english: "When that demon was slain in battle — Sāmba's abode destroyed by the foremost monkey at the urging of the great sages — then was I born of the Wind-god's power, O Maithilī; and a monkey equal to him in might am I."
